mainTopic: Does denying a money claim count as a real כפירה (denial) when there are עדים who could prove the claim anyway? The גמרא tests this with two ברייתות, and both proofs are pushed aside with רבינא's answer.
overview: The גמרא keeps challenging רבה, who says that falsely denying money backed by עדים brings no קרבן. Two ברייתות are answered with רבינא's case of witnesses related through dying wives, and a third is set aside because of רב כהנא's version of its wording. A fourth ברייתא, comparing a נזיר טמא, proves there were valid עדים, and רבה is refuted. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that denying money backed by עדים makes one liable, but a debt backed by a שטר is exempt. רב פפא's reason, that witnesses may die, is rejected. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains instead that a שטר is a lien on land, and no קרבן comes for denying a lien on land, which shows that רבי יוחנן also exempts witnesses about land. רבי ירמיה asks whether this matches the dispute of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן about a stolen field, and רבי אבהו answers that the one who exempts could even follow רבי אליעזר. Finally, רב פפא and רב פפי, both quoting רבא, debate whether the משנה shows that a stolen slave is treated like land.

steps.title: The second set of witnesses was available
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that in the ברייתא of two sets of עדים, the second set was available to testify. Yet the first set's denial still counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the second set of witnesses was standing there, ready to testify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה, who says that denying money backed by עדים is not a real denial. In the ברייתא of two sets of עדים, the second set could have testified, yet the first set is still held liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if the first set of עדים falsely denies knowing testimony and then the second set denies too, both sets are liable. But when the first set denied, the claim could still have been proven through the second set. So it looks like a denial of a money claim counts even when other witnesses exist.

keyTerms.meaning: is standing / is available
the second (set of witnesses)
a set (group) of witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the second set is liable. The question is why the FIRST set is liable when the claim could still be proven through the second set.

phrases.english: But the second set is standing ready!
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא of two sets of witnesses who both denied knowing testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether a denial of a money claim that has witnesses counts as כפירה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a denial of money that has witnesses still counts as a real denial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of two sets of עדים, where the first set is liable even though the second set was available.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that denying money backed by עדים does not count as כפירה and brings no קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the first set denied, the claim could still be proven through the second set. Even so, the first set is liable, so a denial counts even when other witnesses exist.

steps.title: The second set was related through dying wives
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that when the first set denied, the second set was unfit to testify. They were related through their wives, who were dying but still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The case here is one where, at the time the first set denied, the witnesses of the second set were related to one another through their wives, and their wives were dying. You might have thought that since most dying people die, the witnesses should already count as fit. The ברייתא teaches us that right now the wives are still alive and have not died.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes the proof away. He says the second set was not really available, because at that moment they were not allowed to testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives cannot testify together. These men were related through their wives, so as long as the wives were alive, the men were unfit witnesses. Even though the wives were גוססות and most such people die, we go by the present: they are alive now. So when the first set denied, there truly were no other valid עדים, and the ברייתא proves nothing about a claim that has witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrowed reading of a source)
related through their wives
dying, in their final moments
you might have said / you might have thought
it teaches us
most dying people end up dying

steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's answer becomes the tool the גמרא uses again in the next step, so it is worth understanding well.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where the second set was
at the time of the first set's denial
related through their wives,
and their wives were dying.
You might have said:
Most dying people go on to die;
so it teaches us:
right now, at any rate, they are alive
and have not died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by setting the ברייתא in a case where the second set was not valid at the time.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Defends רבה against the challenge from this ברייתא only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the second set was valid witnesses at the time of the first denial. In רבינא's case they were relatives and unfit.

steps.title: The homeowner who claimed a thief took the deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. A שומר who falsely swore that a thief stole the deposit brings an אשם even when witnesses later testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A homeowner who claimed that a thief stole a deposit, swore to it, then admitted, and witnesses came. If he admitted before the witnesses came, he pays the principal, plus a fifth, and brings an אשם. If he admitted after the witnesses came, he pays double and brings an אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to challenge רבה. In this case a man swears falsely about a deposit, witnesses exist, and he still brings an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were witnesses who knew the item was not stolen, and yet his false oath still makes him bring an אשם. That suggests a denial of money counts as כפירה even when witnesses could prove the claim. The difference in payment depends only on when he admitted: before the witnesses, he pays קרן and חומש; after them, he pays כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: the claim that a thief stole the item
a deposit left with someone to watch
the principal plus an added fifth
a guilt-offering
double payment

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not about the payments. It is about the אשם, which he brings in both cases even though there were witnesses.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A homeowner who claimed
phrases.notes: He is the one watching someone else's item.

phrases.english: that a thief stole a deposit,
and swore, and admitted, and witnesses came;

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא בָּאוּ עֵדִים הוֹדָה –
phrases.english: if he admitted before witnesses came,
he pays principal and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
If he admitted after witnesses came,
he pays double payment and brings a guilt-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁטָּעַן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב בְּפִקָּדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a denial of money that has witnesses still counts as a real denial, making him liable for an אשם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of a שומר who made a false טענת גנב with an oath and brings an אשם even though witnesses exist.

steps.title: Answer the second proof the same way as רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא also refers to witnesses who were unfit when he swore, just as רבינא explained.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, explain it as רבינא did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof using the same answer it gave for the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the homeowner swore, the witnesses were related through dying wives, so they could not testify at that moment. By the time they came to court, the wives had died and the witnesses had become fit. So this ברייתא also has no valid witnesses at the time of the oath, and רבה's view survives for now. Steps 7 and 8 later refute him.

keyTerms.meaning: here too
like רבינא (explained)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason. In each ברייתא, at the moment of the denial or oath, the witnesses were relatives through wives who were dying but still alive, so they were not valid. Neither source shows that a denial counts when valid witnesses already exist.

phrases.english: Here too, as Ravina explained.
phrases.notes: The witnesses were relatives through dying wives when he swore, so they were not fit until later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבינא's answer from step 2 to reject the proof of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the homeowner ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the witnesses were valid at the time of the oath. With רבינא's setup, they were unfit relatives then.

steps.title: רבינא's proof from the lashes in the oath-on-a-deposit ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a ברייתא that gives מלקות for a deliberate שבועת הפקדון and an אשם for an accidental one. מלקות needs עדים, so the same case has עדים and still brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. An oath on a deposit is more severe than an oath of testimony. For doing it on purpose a person gets lashes, and for doing it by mistake he brings an אשם worth silver shekels. Since it says he gets lashes, there must be witnesses. Yet it still says that by mistake he brings an אשם!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings another ברייתא to challenge רבה, who holds that denying money backed by עדים does not obligate a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות can only be given when there are עדים. The ברייתא gives מלקות and an אשם for the same oath, so it seems to be talking about a case with עדים. Even so, the denial still brings an אשם, which goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A false oath denying that one holds someone else's money or deposit
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by mistake, without knowing
Lashes (מלקות)
A guilt-offering worth at least two silver shekels
By implication, we can infer

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi,
Come and hear:
An oath on a deposit is more severe than it
phrases.notes: "It" means the oath of testimony (שבועת העדות), which the ברייתא was just discussing.

phrases.english: for one is liable to lashes for doing it on purpose,
and for doing it by mistake, a guilt-offering worth silver shekels.
Since it says he gets lashes,
that implies there are witnesses;
phrases.notes: Lashes are only given when witnesses saw the act and warned him first.

phrases.english: and yet it says: for doing it by mistake
a guilt-offering worth silver shekels!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier ברייתא was answered with 'unfit witnesses', רבינא brings a new source that seems to have valid עדים.
steps.raayaObject: That denying money backed by עדים still brings an אשם (against רבה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that gives מלקות for a deliberate שבועת הפקדון and an אשם for an accidental one

steps.title: רב מרדכי sets the proof aside using רב כהנא's version
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי says this ברייתא is no proof, because רב כהנא teaches it differently. In his version there are no מלקות at all. On purpose or by mistake, one brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to them: Leave that one aside. רב כהנא already told them: I am the one who teaches this ברייתא, and this is how I teach it: whether on purpose or by mistake, he brings an אשם worth silver shekels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי rejects רבינא's proof by showing that the correct wording of the ברייתא never mentions lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole proof depended on the word 'lashes', which showed there were עדים. In רב כהנא's version, both the deliberate and the accidental oath bring an אשם, and there are no lashes. With no lashes, nothing shows there were עדים, so the ברייתא proves nothing against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave that one aside, it is not a proof
I am the one who teaches (recites) this ברייתא
Whether on purpose or by mistake, the same law

phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to them:
Leave that one aside;
for Rav Kahana already told them:
phrases.notes: This refers back to something רב כהנא said earlier, on 37a.

phrases.english: I am the one who teaches it,
and this is how I teach it:
whether on purpose or by mistake,
a guilt-offering worth silver shekels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי: בַּר מִינַּהּ דְּהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5 by correcting the wording of its ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא is removed entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof relied on the word 'lashes', but the correct version of the ברייתא does not mention lashes, so there is no hint of עדים.

steps.title: Challenge from the ברייתא comparing a נזיר טמא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא contrasts a נזיר טמא, who gets מלקות, with שבועת הפקדון, which gets no מלקות. Since the נזיר's lashes require עדים, the case has עדים. The oath-taker escapes only the lashes and still brings a קרבן, so רבה is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: No! If you said so about an impure נזיר, who gets lashes, will you say the same about an oath on a deposit, where he does not get lashes? What is the case? If there are no witnesses, why does the נזיר get lashes? So it must be a case with witnesses. And it teaches that in the oath on a deposit he does not get lashes. Only lashes he does not get, but he does bring a קרבן. This is a refutation of רבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא and argues that it describes a case with עדים. In that case, the oath-taker still brings a קרבן, which is a direct challenge to רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares the two cases side by side, so both must have the same setup. A נזיר only gets lashes when there are עדים, so this setup includes עדים. The ברייתא says the oath-taker escapes only lashes, which means he still brings a קרבן even with עדים, against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר who became impure (from a dead body)
Gets lashes
What is the case? What are the details?
It is obvious
A refutation, a strong challenge that disproves a view

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying the oath-taker is let off completely. The גמרא reads 'he does not get lashes' as limited: he avoids only the lashes, but he still owes a קרבן.

phrases.english: Come and hear: No;
if you said so about an impure nazir
who does get lashes;
will you say so about an oath on a deposit
where he does not get lashes?!
What is the case?
If there are no witnesses,
why does he get lashes?
phrases.notes: "He" here is the נזיר.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that there are witnesses;
and it teaches: will you say so about an oath on a deposit
where he does not get lashes;
it is lashes that he does not get,
but he does bring an offering;
This is a refutation of Rabba!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לֹא; אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּנָזִיר טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous proof was set aside, the גמרא brings a stronger source that clearly involves עדים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that denying money backed by עדים does not obligate a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison with the נזיר shows the case has עדים. The phrase 'he does not get lashes' implies that the oath-taker still brings a קרבן.

steps.title: רבה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the challenge stands. רבה's view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this back-and-forth by admitting that רבה has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'unfit witnesses' answer from earlier cannot work here. The נזיר's lashes prove the עדים were valid, so רבה's position falls.
steps.whatToRemember: The final conclusion: even when there are valid עדים to the money, a person who falsely swears denying it still brings a קרבן שבועת הפקדון, and רבה is refuted.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the challenge in step 7 succeeds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Denying money backed by valid עדים still makes one liable for a קרבן שבועת הפקדון. רבה's view is rejected.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: witnesses mean liable, a document means exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a person who denies a debt backed by עדים is liable for an אשם. If the debt is backed by a שטר, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: One who denies money that has witnesses is liable. If it has a document, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens: רבי יוחנן separates two kinds of proof, עדים and a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עדים, רבי יוחנן agrees with where the גמרא just concluded: the denial counts and he is liable. With a שטר, the denial does not count as denying money, so no קרבן is owed. The next steps explain why the two are different.

keyTerms.meaning: One who denies owing money
A written document, such as a loan document
Liable (here: to bring a קרבן)
Exempt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
One who denies money
that has witnesses is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable to bring the אשם for a false oath on a deposit.

phrases.english: With a document, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הַכּוֹפֵר בְּמָמוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement on a related question: does the kind of proof make a difference?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Denying money backed by עדים makes one liable for an אשם. Denying money backed by a שטר does not.

steps.title: רב פפא asks for רבי יוחנן's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks why רבי יוחנן treats עדים and a שטר differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks why רבי יוחנן's rule makes sense. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both עדים and a שטר prove the debt, so it is not obvious why they should be treated differently. רב פפא asks for the logic behind the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's statement in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עדים lead to liability but a שטר leads to exemption

steps.title: Witnesses can die, but a document stays
steps.stepSummary: עדים might die, so the denial could really have made the owner lose his money. A שטר stays where it is, so denying it could never cancel the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses can die, but a document stays put.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers his own question and explains the difference between עדים and a שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עדים can die, a denial might succeed in the end, so it counts as truly denying money. A שטר stays in place, so the debt can always be collected and the denial has no real effect.

keyTerms.meaning: They tend to die (it can happen that they die)
It stays put; it remains in its place

steps.confusionAlert: Here מָיְיתִי means 'die', from the root מות. It does not mean 'bring', as in אַיְיתֵי.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא's explanation of רבי יוחנן, a denial counts only when it could actually cause the owner to lose money. Witnesses may die, but a שטר stays. The next step challenges this reason.

phrases.english: Witnesses tend to die,
phrases.notes: So the denial might have worked in the end, and he really did try to take the money.

phrases.english: a document stays put.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵדִים עֲבִידִי דְּמָיְיתִי, שְׁטָר הָא מַנַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עדים may die, so the denial could cause a real loss and counts as denying money. A שטר stays in place, so the denial has no effect and he is exempt.

steps.title: A Document Can Also Get Lost
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenges רב פפא's explanation by pointing out that a שטר can also be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said to רב פפא: A document can also get lost!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא attacks the reason from the last step. רב פפא had said a שטר is safe, but a שטר can disappear too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's whole difference between עדים and a שטר was that עדים can die but a שטר stays put. If a שטר can also get lost, then denying a שטר debt could also make the owner lose his money. So the difference falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: a document, here a written loan document
also, too
to get lost, to go missing

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rav Pappa:
A document also can get lost!
phrases.notes: He is answering step 11, where רב פפא said a שטר always stays where it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reason that a שטר is permanent, unlike עדים who may die.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שטר can also be lost, so it is no safer than עדים, and the difference between them disappears.

steps.title: The Real Reason: A Document Creates a Lien on Land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא offers a new reason for רבי יוחנן's ruling: a שטר gives the lender a lien on the borrower's land, and no קרבן is brought for denying a claim on land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: This is רבי יוחנן's reason. A document is a lien on land, and one does not bring an offering for denying a lien on land.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב פפא's reason, רב הונא gives his own reason for why denying a שטר debt brings no קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan written in a שטר automatically ties the borrower's land to the debt. Denying such a debt is like denying a claim on land. The rules of the false oath about a deposit, which bring an אשם, do not apply to land, so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: rather; signals that the earlier explanation is dropped
a lien on land; the borrower's fields are tied to the debt
denial of a claim
an offering brought in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, רבי יוחנן exempts a שטר debt because it is a lien on land, and denying a lien on land brings no קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: The שטר is not exempt because it is safer than עדים. That was רב פפא's reason, and it was just rejected. The new reason is about land.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
This is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan:
because a document is a lien on land,
phrases.notes: A written loan ties the borrower's fields to the debt, so the lender can collect from them.

phrases.english: and one does not bring an offering
for denying a lien on land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הַיְינוּ טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's rejected reason with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing the old one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between עדים and a שטר is that עדים might die while a שטר is permanent.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שטר creates a lien on land, and there is no קרבן for denying a lien on land.

steps.title: Making Witnesses About Land Swear: A Dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר argue about witnesses who falsely swear that they know nothing about a land case. One says they are liable and one says they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If someone makes witnesses about land swear, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree. One says they are liable, and one says they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute about witnesses who falsely swear they have no testimony about land. It does not say which רבי holds which view, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who falsely swear they know nothing usually bring a קרבן. The question is whether this applies when the testimony is about land. The גמרא is about to figure out who holds which side.

keyTerms.meaning: one who makes someone take an oath
witnesses whose testimony is about land
one says

phrases.english: It was stated: One who makes witnesses about land swear —
phrases.notes: The witnesses swore they knew nothing. The question is whether they owe a קרבן for that false oath.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר חַיָּיב, וְחַד אָמַר פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: one says they are liable, and one says they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related dispute about land, which the next step will connect to רב הונא's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר disagree whether witnesses who falsely deny testimony about land are liable. The גמרא does not yet say who holds which view.

steps.title: Proving רבי יוחנן Is the One Who Exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי יוחנן is the one who exempts. He already ruled that denying a שטר debt is exempt, and רב הונא explained that this is because a שטר is a lien on land.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who says exempt. רבי יוחנן said that one who denies money backed by witnesses is liable, but one who denies money backed by a document is exempt. This fits רב הונא the son of רב יהושע's explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יוחנן's earlier ruling, as explained by רב הונא, to figure out his view in the witnesses-about-land dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said רבי יוחנן exempts a שטר because no קרבן comes for denying something tied to land. Following the same logic, רבי יוחנן would also exempt witnesses whose testimony is about land. So he must be the one who says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: it can be concluded; we can figure out
one who denies owing money
and in line with רב הונא's explanation

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof only works because of רב הונא's land-based reason. It shows that his explanation, not רב פפא's, is the one the גמרא builds on.

phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rabbi Yochanan who says exempt —
since Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הַכּוֹפֵר בְּמָמוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: One who denies money that has witnesses is liable,
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 9.

phrases.english: a document — exempt;
and in line with Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: He means: read רבי יוחנן's ruling with רב הונא's reason from step 13, that a שטר is a lien on land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies who holds which view in the dispute from step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן is the one who exempts witnesses about land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own ruling that denying a שטר debt is exempt, as explained by רב הונא: no קרבן comes for denying a lien on land.

steps.title: Confirmed: רבי יוחנן Exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms the conclusion: רבי יוחנן is the one who exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, it may be concluded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof. רבי יוחנן says witnesses about land are exempt, so רבי אלעזר says they are liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single word תסתיים closes this short section by stamping the proof as correct. No one argues with it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says witnesses about land are exempt, and רבי אלעזר says they are liable. This follows from רב הונא's reason that there is no קרבן for claims tied to land.

phrases.english: It may be concluded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the proof in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן exempts witnesses about land, and רבי אלעזר holds them liable.

steps.title: Is This the Same as an Older Dispute?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי אבהו whether the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר is the same as the older dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי אבהו: Shall we say that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר are arguing about the same issue that רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argued about?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה suggests that the new dispute matches an older one. This sets up the source he quotes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לימא offers a possible link that the גמרא will test. If the link holds, רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר are simply following two earlier opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? introduces a suggestion to be tested
a dispute
they disagree

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Abbahu:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנַן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי?
phrases.english: disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנַן קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the dispute settled in steps 14–16 and asks whether it matches an earlier dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the dispute between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר is really the same as the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: The Source: A Stolen Field Flooded by a River
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes the older dispute. If someone steals a field and a river floods it, רבי אליעזר says the thief must give the owner a field. The חכמים say he can tell the owner, "Here is yours in front of you."
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If someone steals a field from his friend and a river floods it, he must provide him with a field. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: He says to him, "Here is yours in front of you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה cites the older dispute he mentioned, so we can see what רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the thief as responsible for the stolen field, so he must make up for the flooded land. The חכמים let him just give back the damaged field as it is. This shows they disagree about whether land is treated like other stolen things.

keyTerms.meaning: one who steals by force
a river flooded it
to provide him with a field
here is yours in front of you

phrases.english: As we learned: One who steals a field from his fellow
and a river flooded it —
he must provide him with a field.
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אוֹמֵר לוֹ ״הֲרֵי שֶׁלְּךָ לְפָנֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: He says to him, "Here is yours in front of you."
phrases.notes: The thief simply hands back the flooded field as it is and pays nothing for the damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן הַגּוֹזֵל שָׂדֶה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וּשְׁטָפָהּ נָהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source of the older dispute mentioned in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That an older dispute exists about whether land is treated like other stolen property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about a stolen field flooded by a river: רבי אליעזר against the חכמים.

steps.title: The Root of Their Dispute: How to Read the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה recalls the explanation already given: רבי אליעזר learns the פסוקים using the method of רבויי ומיעוטי, and the רבנן use the method of כללי ופרטי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: What do they disagree about? רבי אליעזר learns using "includings and excludings," and the רבנן learn using "general rules and details."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה continues by reminding us of an earlier explanation. The dispute about the flooded field comes from two different ways of reading the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבויי ומיעוטי, a general word in the פסוק includes almost everything, so land is included. With כללי ופרטי, the general word is limited to things like the details listed, so land is left out. This explains why רבי אליעזר makes the thief liable for land and the רבנן do not.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree?
includings and excludings; a way of reading פסוקים that includes almost everything
general rules and details; a way of reading פסוקים that limits the general rule to things like the details
learns from the פסוק, explains it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names: רבי אליעזר (in the older dispute) is not רבי אלעזר (who argues with רבי יוחנן). They are two different people.

phrases.english: And we said: About what do they disagree?
Rabbi Eliezer learns using includings and excludings,
and the Rabbis learn using general rules and details.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the dispute quoted in step 18, building toward רבי ירמיה's comparison.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר learns the פסוקים using רבויי ומיעוטי, and the רבנן learn them using כללי ופרטי. This is the root of their dispute about a stolen field.

steps.title: How רבי אליעזר reads the פסוקים as inclusions and limits
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר splits the פסוק into three parts: 'denies to his fellow' includes, 'deposit or loan' limits, and 'anything he swore about' includes again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר learns the פסוקים by the method of including and limiting. 'And he denies to his fellow' includes. 'In a deposit or in a loan' limits. 'Or anything about which he swore' includes again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining רבי אליעזר's method by taking apart the פסוק piece by piece. This sets up the rule that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק gets a job. The broad opening includes, the specific cases limit, and the broad ending includes again. Step 21 explains what that pattern means.

keyTerms.meaning: Inclusions and limits, a method of reading פסוקים where broad words add cases and narrow words limit them
'And he denies to his fellow', the start of the פסוק about falsely denying someone's money
A deposit, an item left with someone for safekeeping
Literally 'placing of the hand': money handed over as a loan or a business deal

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer expounds using inclusions and limits:
"And he denies to his fellow": it included,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21

phrases.english: "in a deposit or in a loan": it limited,
"or anything about which he swore": it went back and included again.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the רבויי ומיעוטי method mentioned in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק follows the pattern include, limit, include.

steps.title: Include, limit, include: everything except שטרות
steps.stepSummary: When the פסוק includes, limits, and includes again, everything is included. The limit only leaves out שטרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it includes, limits, and includes, it includes everything. What did it include? Everything. What did it leave out? Documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the rule for רבי אליעזר's pattern and then asks itself what is in and what is out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this method the second inclusion wins over the limit, so almost everything is covered. The limit only leaves out something very different from a deposit: שטרות, whose worth is only on paper. Since land is not left out, land counts for רבי אליעזר, and that fits his ruling that a thief must give the owner a field.

keyTerms.meaning: It included everything
All things
Documents, such as a written loan contract

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two methods up. In ריבה ומיעט וריבה almost everything is included and only one thing is left out. In כלל ופרט וכלל, coming next, only things like the details are included. The pattern of the פסוק looks the same, but the result is very different.

phrases.english: When it included, limited, and included, it included everything.
What did it include? It included all things;
and what did it leave out? It left out documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule for the pattern laid out in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everything is included except שטרות, so land is included for רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the same פסוקים as general and specific
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'denies to his fellow' as a general phrase, 'deposit, loan, or robbery' as details, and 'anything he swore about' as another general phrase. With that pattern you only include things like the details.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן learn the פסוקים by the method of general phrases and details. 'And he denies to his fellow' is a general phrase. 'In a deposit or in a loan or in robbery' is a detail. 'Or anything about which he swore' goes back and makes a general phrase again. With general, detail, general, you only judge things that are like the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the רבנן and reads the very same words with a different method. It sets up the list of what is included and what is left out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this method the details control the meaning. The general phrases only stretch the law to things that look like the details. So the key question is what the details have in common, and step 23 answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: General phrases and details, a method of reading פסוקים
A general phrase, a detail, and a general phrase again
Like the detail, meaning similar to the specific items listed
Robbery, something taken by force

phrases.english: And the Rabbis expound using general phrases and details:
"And he denies to his fellow": a general phrase,

phrases.aramaic: ״בְּפִקָּדוֹן אוֹ בִתְשׂוּמֶת יָד אוֹ בְגָזֵל״ – פְּרָט,
phrases.english: "in a deposit or in a loan or in robbery": a detail,

phrases.aramaic: ״אוֹ מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִשָּׁבַע עָלָיו״ – חָזַר וְכָלַל.
phrases.english: "or anything about which he swore": it went back and made a general phrase.
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק רבי אליעזר used, just read a different way.

phrases.english: With a general phrase, a detail, and a general phrase,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you only judge things that are like the detail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוקים, side by side with רבי אליעזר's reading in steps 20 and 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With כלל ופרט וכלל, only things like the details are included.

steps.title: Only movable things worth money: land, עבדים and שטרות are left out
steps.stepSummary: The details are movable things that are worth money in themselves. That leaves out land, which cannot move; עבדים, who are compared to land; and שטרות, which can move but are not worth anything as objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the detail is clearly something movable that is itself money, so too anything movable that is itself money is included. Land is left out because it does not move. Slaves are left out because they are compared to land. Documents are left out because even though they move, they are not money in themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names what the details share and uses that to decide what is in and what is out according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two tests: the thing must be movable, and it must be worth money in itself. Land fails the first test, and עבדים are treated like land. שטרות pass the first test but fail the second, because the paper only proves a debt. That is why the רבנן say a thief can tell the owner of a flooded field, 'Here is yours in front of you.'

keyTerms.meaning: Something movable
It is itself money, meaning it has value of its own
Land, real estate
Slaves (עבדים כנענים)
They were compared to land in the פסוקים, so they follow the laws of land

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר (רבויי ומיעוטי): everything is included except שטרות, so land counts. רבנן (כללי ופרטי): only movable things that are worth money in themselves, so land, עבדים and שטרות are all left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רבי ירמיה's question from step 17. Is the argument about land here the same as the argument between רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר about witnesses who falsely swear they know nothing about a land case?

phrases.english: Just as the detail is clearly
something movable that is itself money;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: so too anything movable that is itself money.
Land is left out, because it does not move;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Both mean 'movable.'

phrases.english: slaves are left out, because they are compared to land;

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ שְׁטָרוֹת – שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּטַּלְטְלִין,
phrases.english: documents are left out, because even though they move,
they are not money in themselves.
phrases.notes: The paper only proves that money is owed. The paper itself is worth almost nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the כעין הפרט rule from step 22 to land, עבדים and שטרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only movable things that are worth money in themselves are included. Land, עבדים and שטרות are left out.

steps.title: Do the two arguments line up?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה suggests that the one who makes witnesses liable for a false oath about land follows רבי אליעזר, and the one who exempts them follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says liable holds like רבי אליעזר, and the one who says exempt holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה uses the explanation from the last few steps to suggest that the earlier argument about land is just the same as the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר includes almost everything, even land, so the one who says liable fits him. The רבנן leave out land, so the one who says exempt fits them. This is a suggestion, and the next step tests it.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who says liable
the one who says exempt
the Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: The one who says liable holds like רבי אליעזר,
phrases.notes: This is the earlier argument about witnesses who swear falsely about land.

phrases.english: and the one who says exempt holds like the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דִּמְחַיֵּיב – כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּמַאן דְּפָטַר – כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the רבויי ומיעוטי versus כללי ופרטי explanation to the argument over land.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the liable and exempt opinions about land simply match רבי אליעזר and the רבנן?

steps.title: Even רבי אליעזר may agree to exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says no. The one who says liable must hold like רבי אליעזר. But the one who says exempt can say that even רבי אליעזר agrees here, because the פסוק says 'of anything' and not 'everything.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. The one who says liable holds like רבי אליעזר. But the one who says exempt will tell you: here even רבי אליעזר agrees, because the Torah said 'of anything,' and not 'everything.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו rejects the idea that the two arguments match exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one half of the suggestion holds. Saying liable for land really does need רבי אליעזר's wide reading. But saying exempt does not force you to follow the רבנן, because the word 'מכל' (of anything) shows that not everything is included, even for רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: agrees
the Torah (literally 'the Merciful One')
of anything (only some things)
everything

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבהו does not say the one who exempts must follow the רבנן. He says that person could even hold like רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: He said to him: No;
the one who says liable holds like רבי אליעזר;
but the one who says exempt will tell you:
in this case even רבי אליעזר agrees,
because the Torah said 'of anything'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:כד

phrases.english: and not 'everything.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects half of רבי ירמיה's suggestion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the one who exempts must follow the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'מכל' limits the case even for רבי אליעזר, so exempting does not need the רבנן's method.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying liable for land needs רבי אליעזר. Saying exempt can fit both sides, because 'מכל' means only some things.

steps.title: The משנה mentions a stolen ox but not a stolen slave
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא, quoting רבא, says the wording of the משנה shows that a slave is treated like land. The משנה gives the case 'you stole my ox' and leaves out 'you stole my slave.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: The משנה also shows this. It teaches: 'You stole my ox,' and he says 'I did not steal'; 'I make you swear,' and he said 'Amen,' then he is liable. But it does not teach 'You stole my slave.' Why not? Is it not because a slave is compared to land, and one does not bring a קרבן for denying a lien on land?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings support from the exact wording of the משנה that a false oath about a slave does not bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה chose the example of an ox and left out a slave. That suggests a slave is left out of the rule, because a slave is compared to land, and land does not bring a קרבן. This fits the רבנן's reading from step 23.

steps.title: The 'this is the rule' line may include a stolen slave
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, also quoting רבא, says to look at the end of the משנה. The words 'זה הכלל' must come to add something, and that may be the case of a stolen slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: Look at the last part. This is the rule: anyone who would pay based on his own admission is liable, and anyone who would not pay based on his own admission is exempt. What does 'this is the rule' come to include? Is it not to include 'You stole my slave'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי pushes back on רב פפא's proof by pointing to the general rule at the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'זה הכלל' usually comes to add cases that were not spelled out. If it adds a stolen slave, then the משנה does count a slave, and רב פפא's proof from silence falls apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's proof from the משנה by using the משנה's own general rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה's silence about a slave.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'זה הכלל' at the end of the משנה may include a stolen slave, so leaving it out of the first part proves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's proof is that the משנה is silent about a slave. רב פפי answers that 'זה הכלל' may bring the slave back in.
